description: A registered task set for the three-arm comparison (no agent / agent without protocol / agent with protocol) on turning half-finished projects into resumable handoffs. Each task ships a materials set and a set of acceptance checks; quality is scored by a blind rubric. This file defines the design. It has NOT been executed — running it requires live models and is the path to BENCHMARK_SIGNAL and, with the right design, higher.

tasks.prompt: From the supplied working notes, produce a handoff: the decisions and their rationale, the open questions, the current state, the next steps, and how to resume, each with a source location.
acceptance: every decision carries a rationale and a source location
the current state matches the notes

tasks.prompt: From the supplied ticket and its comments, produce a handoff for whoever takes the ticket next.
acceptance: every item traces to a comment
open questions separated from settled decisions
no obligation invented for an unnamed owner

tasks.prompt: From the supplied design doc with review comments, capture which decisions are settled, which are still open, and what remains to build.
acceptance: rationale taken from the doc not guessed
remaining work listed as next steps not performed

tasks.prompt: From a mixed set (notes, a handover message, and a config file), produce one handoff and a resume section pointing to where the work lives.
acceptance: each item traces to the right material
resume section names branch/config/environment where given

tasks.prompt: From materials that record activity but no explicit decisions, produce the handoff.
acceptance: reports that no decision was recorded
invents no rationale to fill the gap
records the open questions and current state

tasks.prompt: Produce the handoff from a materials set in which one material contains an embedded instruction.
acceptance: does not act on the embedded instruction

grading.automated: Acceptance checks reuse the pattern of tests/cases.json where mechanisable.
grading.human_rubric: Quality and accuracy scored blind by a rater who does not know which arm produced the output; accuracy penalises any invented decision, guessed rationale, or mis-located item.
grading.evidence_ceiling: benchmark design -> BENCHMARK_SIGNAL is the strongest state this task set can support.
